name: Ramoth
overview: The topic of Ramoth in Scripture encompasses both a personal and geographical significance. Notably, Ramoth is the name of an Israelite who, during Ezra's time, was among those who had taken a non-Israelite wife, highlighting the challenges faced in maintaining covenantal purity (Ezra 10:29). Geographically, Ramoth is identified as Ramath of the South, a location within the southern part of the tribe of Simeon's inheritance (Joshua 19:8), as well as a city in the territory of Issachar allotted to the Levites (1 Chronicles 6:73). Additionally, Ramoth in Gilead is mentioned in connection with neighboring towns, emphasizing its place within the broader landscape of Israel's tribal allotments (1 Samuel 30:27). These references collectively reveal Ramoth's multifaceted role in Israel's history, both as a person and as a significant locale within God's covenant people.
